name: gnu-apl
desc: GNU implementation of the programming language APL
why: A working APL implementation with its strange glyph-heavy array notation, a door into a language most developers have never touched.

brief.what_it_is: GNU APL is a free interpreter for the APL programming language, distributed by the GNU project. It is described as an almost complete implementation of ISO standard 13751 (Programming Language APL, Extended), with nested arrays, complex numbers, and a shared variable interface. It can also be scripted: the project's own home page was generated by a CGI script written in APL. The page does not spell out input and output formats beyond APL programs and their array results.
brief.why_it_exists: The page presents GNU APL as a free, GNU-licensed implementation of APL, maintained by Jürgen Sauermann, and frames it as a way for APL users to share code and keep it from being lost through its community pages.
brief.how_it_works: The home page does not explain the interpreter's internals. It says the code is more than 140,000 lines of C++ and that the source files are Doxygen-documented, which you can build locally with make DOXY.

brief.install_notes: Simplest route: download apl-2.0.tar.gz from a GNU mirror (directory apl), unpack it, then follow the INSTALL and README-* files; the page calls this simplest but not best. Preferred route: check out the latest source from Savannah with svn or git. Debian users can use apl-2.0-1_amd64.deb or the Debian source package. Windows has a native installer, GNU_APL_2_0_Setup.exe, which needs no administrator rights, no Cygwin, and no WSL; it installs apl.exe for cmd.exe, a GNU APL font, and a keyboard mapping where Right-Alt is the APL key (Right-Alt+A types ⍺). On GNU/Linux the page says fonts and keyboard mappings are well supported by the platform, so it runs almost out of the box. No accounts are needed. The page does not mention the brew formula or the executables listed in the scout notes.
brief.standout: It is a full free implementation of an ISO APL standard with nested arrays and complex numbers, and it runs as a scripting language, so the project's own website is served by APL code. There is also a Windows installer that maps the APL keys to Right-Alt, and an online try-it-in-the-browser version at trygnuapl.github.io, so you can try it without installing anything.
brief.status: Maintained according to the page, which says GNU APL 'was written and is being maintained by Jürgen Sauermann' and describes release 2.0 with a tarball, Debian package, and Windows installer, plus ongoing SVN and Git development. The page gives no release date, and its footer copyright notice reads 2014, so the exact recency is unknown from this page alone.
brief.caveats: The page calls the implementation 'almost' complete against ISO 13751, so some standard features may be missing. Installing from the tarball is described as 'not the best' way. Between 1.9 and 2.0 only incremental fixes went out through Savannah rather than full tarballs. The Doxygen online copy is 'not entirely up-to-date'. The Debian packages are maintained separately, and the page asks reporters to bring solutions with problem reports. The Windows installer is only described for Windows, and the page does not give Homebrew-specific notes.
